analysis.title: Keysight Technologies Inc. (KEYS): Record orders with strong growth drivers for FY27 and beyond; 4QFY26 wrap
key_insights: Keysight 4QFY26 revenue was $1,994 mn (up 8% qoq, up 41% yoy), versus GS at $1,948 mn and the Street (FactSet) at $1,946 mn, and above the guidance range of $1,930 mn to $1,950 mn. Core revenue was up 36% yoy.
Non-GAAP EBIT margin ex-SBC was ~35.8% versus the Street at 34.5% and GS at 35.0%. Non-GAAP EPS ex-SBC was $3.61 versus GS at $3.39 and the Street at $3.37.

Orders were a record $2,339 mn (up 12% qoq, up 53% yoy as reported, up 49% yoy organically) with a book-to-bill of ~1.17X. GS says some investors may have expected better than seasonal qoq order growth, but the 3Q base was also high.
1QFY27 guidance midpoint is revenue $2,050 mn and non-GAAP EPS $3.66, versus the Street at $1,963 mn and $3.21 and GS prior at $1,927 mn and $3.08.

Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 20% as a base case, implying ~$8.6 bn versus GS prior at ~$8.1 bn and the Street at ~$8.2 bn. Management expects FY27 incremental margins in the mid-to-high 40% range, above its 40% long-term framework.

Management expects 1QFY27 orders to decline mid-single digits sequentially, in line with typical seasonality, and says this does not reflect a change in demand. The company enters FY27 with a record backlog and strong pipeline.
AI bookings in FY26 were ~2.5x FY25. GS estimates this implies about $1.4 bn in FY26.
Demand continues to outpace supply. Capacity has increased for the fourth consecutive quarter, but fully easing supply constraints remains a moving target.

GS maintains its Buy rating. Its thesis rests on exposure to fast-growing markets (AI networking/datacenter, A&D), cyclical improvement in wireless and industrial/auto, and deal integration synergies.
GS sees long-term growth beyond FY27 from 6G R&D (6G slated to come online in 2029 per management), A&D projects, and optical interconnect programs. Recurring revenue was 25% of total in the quarter.
GS raises FY27/28 EPS (inc. SBC) to $13.95/$15.45 from $12.50/$14.05 and introduces an FY29 estimate of $16.45. Excluding SBC, it models FY27/28/29 EPS of $15.40/$16.95/$18.00.

GS cuts its 12-month price target to $464 from $487. The target is now based on 30X (from 35X, reflecting peer multiples) applied to normalized EPS of $15.45 inc. SBC. The stock closed at $281.42, implying 64.9% upside.
Free cash flow was about $465 mn in the quarter (~23% of revenue). Software and services were ~33% of revenue.

market_movers.rationale: GS maintains Buy after a 4QFY26 beat and guidance above the Street, and raises estimates. The target falls to $464 from $487 as the multiple drops to 30X from 35X on peer multiples.

earnings_insights: KEYS 4QFY26 reported 11/19/2026: revenue $1,994 mn vs GS $1,948 mn and Street (FactSet) $1,946 mn. Non-GAAP EPS ex-SBC $3.61 actual vs GS $3.39 and Street $3.37. Non-GAAP EPS inc. SBC $3.35 actual vs GS $3.07.
KEYS 4QFY26 non-GAAP operating margin ex-SBC was 35.8% actual vs GS 35.0% and Street 34.5%. Margin inc. SBC was 33.6% vs GS 32.2%.
KEYS 1QFY27 guidance (company, non-GAAP ex-SBC): revenue $2,040-2,060 mn (midpoint $2,050 mn) vs GS prior $1,927 mn and Street $1,963 mn. EPS $3.63-3.69 vs GS prior $3.08 and Street $3.21.
KEYS FY27 guidance (company base case): about 20% revenue growth, implying ~$8.6 bn vs GS prior ~$8.1 bn and Street ~$8.2 bn.
4QFY26 orders $2,339 mn: Aerospace, Defense & Government $351 mn, Commercial Communications $1,145 mn, Electronic Industrial Solutions Group $498 mn.
risk_factors: Revenue outlook, especially in 5G/6G, EVs/AVs and 800Gb/1.6Tb/3.2Tb, could be lower on weaker end-market trends or share shifts.
Margins could face pricing pressure, tariffs, or the shift to production test, despite software mix helping.
Keysight's ability to keep innovating and lead through R&D and M&A.
